findings.title: UnixFileLock opens lock path with O_TRUNC without O_NOFOLLOW, truncating symlink target
findings.evidence: Root cause: `open_flags = os.O_RDWR | os.O_TRUNC` (line 41) is passed to `os.open(self.lock_file, open_flags, self._context.mode)` (line 44) with no `os.O_NOFOLLOW`. os.open resolves symlinks, so if the lock file path is a symlink to a victim-owned file, acquiring the lock truncates that file to zero bytes under the victim process's privileges. Reachability: an attacker with write access to the directory holding the lock (e.g. the common pattern of a lock file under /tmp or a shared workspace) pre-creates `lock_file` as a symlink to a sensitive target the victim can write (e.g. ~/.bashrc, source tree, database). When the victim calls FileLock(...).acquire() -> _acquire(), the O_TRUNC open follows the link and destroys the target's contents; additionally `ensure_directory_exists` makes the parent dir, and if the symlink is dangling `Path(self.lock_file).exists()` (line 42) is False so O_CREAT is added and the attacker-chosen target path is created. The truncation happens before `fcntl.flock` (line 48) is attempted, so it occurs even when the attacker holds the flock and the victim's acquire fails, and the blocking poll loop in _api.py:329-344 re-runs _acquire() every poll_interval, repeatedly re-truncating. The subsequent `os.fchmod(fd, self._context.mode)` (line 46) also chmods the symlink target to 0o644. No link check (lstat/O_NOFOLLOW) is performed anywhere in _acquire, so this is a reachable arbitrary-file-truncation primitive; the file itself is never otherwise written, so truncation is the sole, intended-looking but unsafe effect.

findings.title: WindowsFileLock opens lock path with O_TRUNC without reparse-point protection
findings.evidence: Same pattern as the Unix lock: flags `os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT | os.O_TRUNC` (lines 22-26) are passed to `os.open(self.lock_file, flags, self._context.mode)` (line 28) with no check that the lock path is not a symlink/reparse point. On Windows an attacker who can create a symlink (developer mode / SeCreateSymbolicLinkPrivilege) or place the lock file in a shared directory that the victim process locks will cause the victim's `acquire()` (WindowsFileLock is the default FileLock on win32, see __init__.py:34) to open through the link with O_TRUNC and truncate the target file before msvcrt.locking is attempted. Precondition is stronger than on Unix because symlink creation normally requires privilege, hence low severity, but the unsafe open (write+truncate through an attacker-controlled link) is the same root cause with no lstat/readlink guard in _acquire.
